data.outcome_summary: PIRLS 2021 is a fourth-grade reading achievement assessment conducted every five years, with the 2021 cycle providing 20 years of trend results. The assessment was administered in 57 countries and 8 benchmarking entities, with data collection occurring over two years during COVID-19 disruptions. PIRLS 2021 introduced a transition to digital assessment for a subset of countries and implemented a group adaptive design that assigns students to booklets combining easy/medium/difficult text and item sets, improving measurement precision and reducing item non-response. Scaling procedures place results on the PIRLS trend scale using concurrent calibration and linking designs, including population-based linking between digital main and bridge samples. The report also documents quality assurance steps (translation verification, standardized procedures, and international quality assurance visits) and explains how delayed testing countries are annotated, emphasizing that PIRLS cannot establish causal effects of COVID-19 on achievement.
